default.notes: A visitor visa must be obtained in advance from an Antigua and Barbuda High Commission, embassy or consulate. Antigua and Barbuda waives visas for well over 100 nationalities, so check the Immigration Department's current exempt list before assuming you need one.

groups.notes: CARICOM nationals move freely within the community — visitors are normally granted a six-month stay on arrival, and skilled nationals with a CARICOM certificate may live and work.

No visa is needed, but The Bahamas and Haiti take part in CARICOM's free-movement arrangements only partially — the automatic six-month community stay is not guaranteed, so confirm the length of stay you will be given before booking.

No visa needed — visitors are normally admitted for up to six months, with the exact period set by the immigration officer from your ticket and accommodation. Extensions are handled by the Immigration Department in St John's.
Chinese citizens enter without a visa under the bilateral waiver agreement, commonly for up to 30 days — confirm the current allowance before booking.
Russian citizens are covered by a bilateral visa-waiver agreement, usually reported as up to 90 days — confirm with an Antigua and Barbuda mission before travelling.

AG.notes: Home country — no entry requirements for citizens of Antigua and Barbuda.

IN.notes: Indian passport holders are not clearly listed as visa-exempt — plan on applying for a visitor visa in advance. Some sources report a short-stay Commonwealth waiver, so confirm with the Antigua and Barbuda High Commission before booking.
